title: 2002 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 7
statement: \(p\) and \(q\) are primes such that the numbers \(p+q\) and \(p+7 q\) are both squares. Find the value of \(p\).

solutions.text: 2. Writing \(x^{2}=p+q, y^{2}=p+7 q\), we have \(6 q=y^{2}-x^{2}=(y-x)(y+x)\). Since \(6 q\) is even, one of the factors \(y-x, y+x\) is even, and then the other is as well; thus \(6 q\) is divisible by \(4 \Rightarrow q\) is even \(\Rightarrow q=2\) and \(6 q=12\). We may assume \(x, y\) are both taken to be positive; then we must have \(y-x=2, y+x=6 \Rightarrow x=2\), so \(p+2=2^{2}=4 \Rightarrow p=2\) also.
